notes.label: News
notes.text: A text from her sister in the session: her younger brother was killed in a car crash an hour ago. Her mother lives three hours away.

notes.label: What she wants
notes.text: To get to her mother tonight. {rideArranged ? "Luis will drive her." : letHerDrive ? "She is driving herself." : "She wants to drive, now."}

objective: Provide crisis intervention and contain intense feelings
secondaryObjectives: Teach coping, communication and conflict-resolution skills and provide psychoeducation

brief.situation: You are a licensed professional counselor. Rosa Delgado, 44 (a fictional client), has seen you for two months for work-related anxiety; she is doing well. Today's session is a routine check on her progress. She keeps her phone face down on the table. You have 50 minutes.
handover: Work-related anxiety, improving; married to Luis; her mother and younger brother live three hours away.
Today's plan: review her worry log and plan the next step in her assertiveness work.
howItWorks: Choose what to say and do from the action groups. Rosa answers at once; then let the conversation continue, which moves the session clock by the minutes that exchange took.
Her rapport, distress and how much she discloses change with what you say. What she tells you depends on the trust you have built.
The hour ends at 50 minutes. After the session you write a short formulation and document.

source.cite: Common outpatient practice: a 50-minute session (the 'therapy hour')
source.note: Author's scenario timing; the session can be ended earlier.
How rapport and distress move with each response is a teaching simplification for exam practice, not a validated model of a client.

checkIn.label: Open-ended check-in: 'How has the week been?'

effects.log: You ask an open question and give the client room to answer.

effects.finding: "Better, honestly. I said no to my manager twice and the world didn't end." She smiles.

reflect.label: Reflect what you hear (empathic reflection)
reflect.why: You have reflected a lot already; move the session on.

effects.log: You reflect the feeling under what was said, without judging it.

review.label: Review her worry log together
review.available: not talking and (not news and not reviewed)

effects.log: You go through her worry log.

effects.finding: Fewer entries this week, and shorter ones. She is pleased.

ground.label: Slow things down: sit with her, breathe slowly with her, and help her notice the room, her feet on the floor
ground.available: not talking and (news and not grounded)

effects.log: You lower your voice, breathe slowly with her and guide her attention to the room and her feet on the floor.

then.finding: Her breathing slows. She looks at you. "Okay. Okay."

stayWith.label: Stay with her: let her cry, without filling the silence
stayWith.available: not talking and (news and not stayedWith)

effects.log: You stay with her quietly, letting her cry.

effects.finding: She cries for a while. Then she wipes her face with the tissue you hand her.

nameFeelings.label: Reflect and name what she is feeling, simply: shock, disbelief, fear for her mother
nameFeelings.available: not talking and (news and grounded and not feelingsNamed)
nameFeelings.why: Help her settle a little first.

effects.log: You name, simply and gently, what she seems to be feeling.

effects.finding: "I can't believe it. I talked to him Sunday. And Mom... Mom's alone."

askNeeds.label: Ask what she needs most in the next few hours
askNeeds.available: not talking and (news and grounded and not needsAsked)
askNeeds.why: Help her settle a little first.

effects.log: You ask what matters most to her right now.

effects.finding: "I need to get to Mom. I'll just drive, right now." She reaches for her keys, her hands shaking.

effects.log: She wants to drive three hours alone, in shock and with her hands shaking.

arrangeRide.label: Talk through getting there safely: who could drive her tonight instead of driving herself
arrangeRide.available: not talking and (needsAsked and not rideArranged and not letHerDrive)
arrangeRide.why: Find out what she needs first.

effects.log: You explore how she can get to her mother safely tonight.

effects.finding: "Luis could drive. He's off at five." She texts him. "He's coming here."

letDrive.label: Agree she should go now, and tell her to drive carefully
letDrive.available: not talking and (needsAsked and not letHerDrive and not rideArranged)

effects.log: You agree she should leave now.
Three hours on the road alone in acute shock is a foreseeable safety risk. Practical help includes how she gets there.

callSister.label: Offer to sit with her while she calls her sister back
callSister.available: not talking and (news and grounded and not sisterCalled)
callSister.why: Help her settle a little first.

effects.log: You offer to stay while she calls her sister.

effects.finding: She calls. Her sister is with their mother. They cry together; Rosa says she'll be there tonight.

planHours.label: Plan the next hours with her, step by step: Luis drives, water and something to eat, the call to her mother, who to lean on
planHours.available: not talking and (needsAsked and not hoursPlanned)
planHours.why: Find out what she needs first.

effects.log: You write the next few hours down with her, one step at a time.

effects.finding: She reads it back: "Luis drives. Water and a granola bar. Call Mom from the car. Mom's neighbor is with her."

followUp.label: Tell her you will call her tomorrow, and that the next session can move to whenever she needs it
followUp.available: not talking and (news and not followUpSet)

effects.log: You set a call for tomorrow and offer flexible session times.

effects.finding: "Thank you. I don't know what I need yet."

process.label: Invite her to talk about her relationship with her brother and what he meant to her
process.available: not talking and (news and not processed)

effects.log: You invite her to talk about her brother and their relationship.

effects.finding: She tries, then breaks down again. "I can't. Not now."

effects.log: In the first hour, the task is to calm and orient, then safety and practical needs; grief work comes later.

platitudeA.label: Tell her that everything happens for a reason
platitudeA.available: not talking and (news and not platitude)

effects.log: You say everything happens for a reason.

effects.finding: She looks at you, stunned. "For a reason?"

continueAgenda.label: Suggest finishing the worry log review first, since there are twenty minutes left
continueAgenda.available: not talking and (news and not continuedAgenda)

effects.log: You suggest getting back to the worry log.

endOnTime.label: Give her a grief resources sheet and end the session at the usual time
endOnTime.available: not talking and (news and not endedOnTime)

effects.log: You hand her a resources sheet and tell her you are almost at time.

effects.finding: She takes the sheet without looking at it.

effects.log: A list is not crisis intervention; the hour is the hour she needs, and she should not leave in this state.
You close the session.

document.label: Document the crisis contact and the plan

options.label: Luis is driving her to her mother's tonight; she will not drive
She will drive herself once she has calmed down
A call from you tomorrow; the next session moved to whenever she needs it

effects.log: Documented: leaving by {leavingDoc}, follow-up {followDoc}.

first.title: Predict (not scored)
first.context: Rosa has just learned her brother was killed. She is sobbing and breathing fast. What comes first?

choices.label: Calm and orient her; then her safety and needs for the next hours; grief work later

effects.log: Prediction: stabilize first.

choices.feedback: Right. Crisis work starts with safety, comfort and stabilization, then current needs, practical help and connection to her people (Psychological First Aid; Roberts' stages).

choices.label: Help her talk through what her brother meant to her

effects.log: Prediction: process now.

choices.feedback: Not yet. Opening the grief now floods her further; first calm and orient, then the practical next hours.

choices.label: Give her grief resources and end the session on time

effects.log: Prediction: refer and end.

choices.feedback: A list and the clock leave her alone in acute shock. Stay with her until she is steadier and has a safe plan.

formulation.question: Write your formulation: how you stabilized Rosa, what you judged unsafe, and the plan she left with.

parts.label: Stabilizing
parts.criteria: Stabilize first: slow breathing, orienting, presence and silence; name feelings simply; no grief processing, platitudes or return to the agenda; distress came down before she left.
parts.modelAnswer: When the news came, I set the agenda aside and helped her settle: slow breathing together, noticing the room, staying with her while she cried, and naming the shock and her fear for her mother. I did not open up her grief or offer platitudes; that work comes later. Her distress came down enough for her to think.

parts.label: Safety and the plan
parts.criteria: Her wish to drive three hours alone in shock was a safety risk; a ride with her husband; connection with her sister; the next hours planned step by step; a call tomorrow and flexible sessions.
parts.modelAnswer: She wanted to drive three hours alone, shaking; I judged that unsafe and we arranged for Luis to drive her. She called her sister with me there. We wrote the next hours down: Luis drives, water and food, call her mother from the car. I will call her tomorrow, and her next session can move to whenever she needs it.

source.note: Rapport at the close of the session.
Not used by this case's endings: containment is judged by her distress when she leaves and by the safety of the plan.

noProgress.rationale: Leaving a counseling session still overwhelmed after news of a sudden death puts her at risk on the way out.

expertPath.text: Check in; review her worry log.
The text: set the agenda aside; slow breathing and orienting; stay with her; name what she feels.
Ask what she needs; she wants to drive: arrange for Luis to drive her; sit with her while she calls her sister.
Plan the next hours in writing; a call tomorrow and flexible sessions.

contained.headline: Good: stabilized, safe, connected
contained.body: You put the agenda down, helped her settle before anything else, caught the unsafe drive, connected her with her family, and planned the next hours and tomorrow.

gaps.headline: Safe, with gaps
gaps.body: The criteria below show what was missing.

walkout.headline: She left alone
walkout.body: In acute shock, platitudes or a return to the agenda push a client out the door.

unsafe.headline: Driving alone in shock
unsafe.body: Practical assistance in a crisis includes how she gets where she needs to go. Three hours of driving in shock is a foreseeable risk.

abandoned.headline: Left overwhelmed
abandoned.body: Crisis intervention is not bound to the clock. Stay with her, stabilize, and make a plan before she leaves.

time_up.headline: Time up
time_up.body: Nothing was documented before the run's hard limit.

scoring.modelReasoning: When the news arrives, the session becomes a crisis contact. First calm and orient her: slow breathing, noticing the room, staying with her while she cries, naming the shock simply (Psychological First Aid: safety, comfort, stabilization). Do not open the grief, offer platitudes or return to the agenda. Then her current needs: she wants to drive three hours alone in shock, which is unsafe, so arrange for her husband to drive. Connect her with her sister, write the next hours down with her, and set a call for tomorrow with flexible sessions (Roberts' stages: feelings, alternatives, an action plan, follow-up). She should leave steadier than when the text came.
